Question_text: Saltan makes a range of cars. The level of inventory is too high so it plans to decrease production at its factory. Employees were told the business needs to reduce the size of its workforce as competition is increasing. The trade union is not happy that 360 of the 1200 skilled full time employees at Saltan will be made redundant. A trade union spokeswoman said: 'Saltan should reduce the number of hours of every employee rather than reduce the number of jobs.' Saltan's Operations Director is considering ways to increase efficiency in the factory.
Sub_topic: Trade unions: definition, effects of membership
Situations for downsizing: automation, reduced demand
Increasing efficiency: automation, technology, labour skills

Parts.part_text: What is meant by a 'trade union'?
Identify two situations (other than increasing competition) when a business might have to reduce the size of its workforce.
Identify and explain two possible problems for Saltan of having a high level of inventory.
Identify and explain two ways Saltan could improve efficiency.
Do you think Saltan should reduce the number of working hours for every employee rather than reduce the number of jobs? Justify your answer.

Question_text: F&G is a leading fashion retailer. It has 20 shops in country C. The business uses market segmentation. Its target market is men aged between 25 and 40 years old. The Marketing Director has been looking at the marketing data shown in Table 1. She is worried that the amount the business spends on marketing is not cost effective. She would like to close down all F&G shops and just use e-commerce. Table 1 Year | Total value of the men's clothing market | F&G's market share | F&G's marketing budget 2015 | $500m | 15% | $25m 2016 | $700m | 12% | $40m
Sub_topic: How/why segment: age, socio-economic, location, gender

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'marketing budget'?
Calculate the value of F&G's revenue in 2016.
Identify and explain two benefits of market segmentation to F&G.
Identify and explain two possible reasons why the amount F&G spends on marketing might not be cost effective.
Do you think F&G should close down all its shops and just use e-commerce? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Alex and Raul are business partners. They started a bicycle repair business with their own savings as the bank would not give them a loan. Raul does most of the repair work, while Alex manages the accounts. Alex is surprised that the business has made a small profit in the first year. 'We can use this profit to expand. I don't know why people think we would benefit from having a business plan. Much of the demand for our repair business comes from our friends who own bicycles.' Table 2: Extract from balance sheet as at 31 March 2016 ($) Non-current assets: 3000 Current assets: 2500 Current liabilities: 2000 Non-current liabilities: 1500
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Contents of business plan, assistance to entrepreneurs

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'non-current liabilities'?
Calculate the working capital.
Identify and explain two possible reasons why working capital is important to Alex and Raul's business.
Identify and explain two benefits to Alex of having a business partner.
Do you think Alex and Raul need a business plan for the business to be successful in the future? Justify your answer.

Question_text: KLG is based in country X. It specialises in making electrical parts which it sells to washing machine manufacturers in country X. The Managing Director is planning to relocate to country Y, which is a low-cost country. She said: 'This will allow us to pay employees low wages for working long hours as there are few legal controls on employment and health and safety. KLG cannot be both ethical and profitable. Changes in exchange rates and import tariffs might cause us problems when we start exporting.'
Unit: UNIT 6: External influences on business activity
Sub_topic: Impact on importers, exporters: prices, competitiveness, profitability
Legal controls: contracts, unfair dismissal, discrimination, health/safety, minimum wage
Ethical issues: profit vs ethics conflicts

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'import tariff'?
Identify two benefits to KLG of specialisation.
Explain how a change in exchange rates might affect KLG when exporting.
Identify and explain two factors (other than exchange rates and import tariffs) that KLG should consider when deciding where to relocate.
The Managing Director believes that 'KLG cannot be both ethical and profitable.' Do you agree? Justify your answer.
